newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 7.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on July 7:

PASADENA, CALIFORNIA - The Sojourner, the first mobile geologist on Mars, nosed around the jagged Martian surface with instructions to investigate its first target: a football-sized rock dubbed "Barnacle Bill."
MEXICO CITY - Preliminary results from voter exit polls showed Mexican leftist opposition candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas with a decisive lead in the election of Mexico City's mayor.

WASHINGTON - In President Bill Clinton's second term, Samuel "Sandy" Berger's job is not just statecraft, but stagecraft. And a principal goal of the staging is to convince skeptics that Clinton has big ideas about the world and is capable of implementing them.

WASHINGTON - Forty-two children from the southern region of Belarus, near the crippled Chernobyl nuclear reactor, arrived in the Washington area in June for a brief respite in a relatively contamination-free environment.

WASHINGTON - Syracuse University and major other colleges are facing a budget crunch as they try to comply with Title IX, the federal law passed in June 1972 that prohibits sex discrimination in programs at institutions that receive federal funds.
HONG KONG - Cambodia appeared to be sliding into chaos with the armies of the two feuding prime ministers battling with rockets, artillery and small arms in the streets of the capital, Phnom Penh.
